title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp: four-limb scalar recurrence, two-limb baby indices

claims.statement: For uniform s in 1..r-1 on BLS12-381 G1, with public powers A_i=[s^i]P0 for i=1..n at n=2^20, the deterministic four-limb scalar recurrence in proof.md recovers s with probability 1 using at most 2^130 total target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing, sorting, lookup and verification. The baby index is two 64-bit limbs because the stage-1 width M satisfies 2^117 < M < 2^118. Peak memory is at most 2^126 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^130 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is at most 2^0 bytes and is included in memory. No heuristic. The bound applies when n divides r-1 (true at the scoring n) and the attack reads A_1 and A_n.

experiments.purpose: On a prime-order multiplicative toy group whose 2-power dividing the order shares a gcd greater than 1 with the cofactor, recover every secret by the two-stage recurrence. Also check the production integers: M is the ceiling square root of (r-1)/2^20, M fits in two limbs and not in one, and 7 is a primitive root modulo r. Not a production cost measurement.
